Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. We're pulling together a ZIP with a diagram and an egress snapshot. A couple quick clarifications so we give you the right artifacts:

1) Is HealthBridge planning to use a VPC peering (routing) setup or prefer an AWS PrivateLink/Interface Endpoint pattern? We can document both but would tailor recommendations to your preferred topology.
2) For the allowlist: do you need a single daily snapshot, or a rolling 7-day export of observed egress IPs?

High level for transparency: Redwood's hosted offering uses regional pools and (depending on customer choice) either VPC peering or interface endpoints. For peering we expose a set of egress SNAT IPs from the peering host; for PrivateLink we present private ENIs in your VPC and avoid public egress entirely for model traffic. We'll include pros/cons in the packet.

I'll loop in Neha (security) and Laura (networking) for the technical evidence.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — VPC peering / allowlist evidence request

Jordan — attaching the requested evidence bundle; summary below.

(Attachment: sig-evidence-pack-20270322.pdf (PDF) — includes topology rationale, configuration snippets, and signed network statement)
(Attachment: redwood-vpc-peering-diagram-20270322.png (PNG) — simplified peering + route table view)
(Attachment: egress-ip-snapshot-20270322.csv (CSV) — current public SNAT IPs observed for us-west-2 peering hosts)

Summary (quick bullets):
- Recommended initial topology: VPC peering in us-west-2 for HealthBridge development and pre-prod. PrivateLink preferred for production deployments where you want zero public egress for model traffic. Both are supported.
- Egress IPs: see CSV (10 IPs). We publish an allowlist snapshot daily; if an IP changes we follow a scheduled rotation process and provide notice via the HubSpot security ticket (link included).
- Rotation policy: ephemeral egress IPs are recycled on a quarterly schedule by default. For customers that require more frequent rotation we can support monthly or weekly rotations; changes >1/month require a short maintenance window (15–30m) during which we announce an IP swap and provide the new snapshot.
- Required inbound ports: only 443/TCP for model RPC and 443/TCP for health checks. No additional inbound port ranges are required for standard peering.
- SNAT/source-port behavior: outbound source ports will be ephemeral (1024-65535). We don't require static source ports.

Operational notes:
- We recommend adding a DNS-based fallback for client connections (redwood-usw2-primary.redwood-inference.com) so we can fail over between internal clusters without changing your allowlist if you prefer less frequent whitelisting.
- Attachment: peer-config.txt (included in the PDF appendix) shows example route table entries and security group rules.

Let me know if you want a short RFC with timelines for a one-off rotation during your cutover.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Network Architect | Redwood Inference
